sources.title: Calculus of Variations, Oberwolfach Report 37/2024; Radu Ignat contribution
sources.inspection: Cached official PDF parsed; printed pages 2133 and 2136 rendered and visually inspected. Official URL independently opened through web tool. Definition is C1 convex W, positive away from 0; Question 2 inherits it.

sources.title: Minimality of vortex solutions to Ginzburg–Landau type systems for gradient fields in the unit ball in dimension N>=4
sources.status: Published 24 January 2025, Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 249, article 14.
sources.inspection: Web PDF and HTML inspected: Theorem 1, Section 1.1, Theorem 5, and Appendix A. C2 convex W in the full theorem; N=2,3 excluded from that result. Publisher publication record checked.

sources.title: Global minimality of the degree-one Ginzburg-Landau vortex solution in the unit ball in dimensions n>=2
sources.inspection: Web abstract, HTML and PDF opened; energy definition, admissible H1 class, Theorem 1.1, comparison identities, Lemmas 2.1–2.3, Proposition 2.4 and theorem deduction inspected. Scope is the standard quartic energy. Complete 30-page proof not independently certified.

sources.title: On Brezis' open problem 2.2
sources.inspection: Web record, introduction, standard-energy definition, Theorem 1.1 and rescaling read. Provides planar precursor credited by Ignat–Nguyen.

sources.title: Local minimality of RN-valued and SN-valued Ginzburg–Landau vortex solutions in the unit ball BN
sources.status: Published, Annales de l Institut Henri Poincare C 41 (2024), 663–724.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record read; primary PDF opened. Used only for standard-model local minimality / nonnegative second variation, not global uniqueness.

sources.title: The Ginzburg-Landau system with general potential: maximum principle and gradient estimates
sources.inspection: Abstract checked. It is about critical-point bounds and a conditional convergence regime, not the desired general-potential global minimization theorem.

sources.title: Finite Potential Energy for Entire Solutions of the Planar Ginzburg–Landau Equation
sources.inspection: Introduction and Theorem 1.1 checked. Entire planar potential-energy result is a different target and not counted as resolving the bounded-ball question.
